data.title: The Grammar Engine
data.description: High-precision calibration of irregular forms and fixed prepositional phrases.

sections.explain: You are 'interested IN' something. Never 'on' or 'at'.

words.word: I am very interested in learning Italian.
I am very interested at learning Italian.
I am very interested on learning Italian.

sections.explain: In English, you are 'good AT' a skill or activity.

words.word: He is very good at playing the piano.
He is very good in playing the piano.
He is very good for playing the piano.

sections.explain: You are married 'TO' someone. 'Married with' is a direct translation error.

words.word: She has been married to him for ten years.
She has been married with him for ten years.
She has been married by him for ten years.

sections.explain: 'Listen' must be followed by 'to' when there is an object.

words.word: I like to listen to classical music.
I like to listen classical music.
I like to listen at classical music.
I have never flown in a private jet.
I have never flew in a private jet.
I have never flyed in a private jet.

sections.explain: The verb 'avoid' must be followed by the -ing form (gerund).

words.word: You should avoid eating too much sugar.
You should avoid to eat too much sugar.
You should avoid eat too much sugar.

sections.explain: The verb 'decide' is followed by 'to' + infinitive.

words.word: We decided to go to the beach.
We decided going to the beach.
We decided for go to the beach.
He has thrown the ball over the fence.
He has threw the ball over the fence.
He has throwed the ball over the fence.

sections.sentence: Which sentence describes a regret correctly?
sections.explain: To express regret about the past, use 'wish' + 'had' + past participle.

words.word: I wish I had studied more for the test.
I wish I studied more for the test.
I wish I would have studied more for the test.

sections.explain: The phrase 'looking forward to' is always followed by -ing.

words.word: I am looking forward to meeting you.
I am looking forward to meet you.
I am looking forward for meeting you.
